diagnostic_evidence.quote: For all other tuples $f$, we have $\deg X > r$ and there exist linear space of projective dimension $r-1$ that intersects $X$ in more than $r$ real points, see~\cite[Theorem 1.6]{ranestad2024real}.

issues.failure_explanation: The 'otherwise' branch claims r(f) = min{n_col^f, n_codim^f} for every tuple f other than the two-ones case. For degenerate tuples with at most one nonzero entry equal to 1 (e.g. f=(1,0,...,0) for l=1, or f=0), X is a linear projective space: n_codim^f = N-1-sum_{f_i≠0}(m_i-1) = 0 and deg X = 1. The formula then yields r(f) = min{n_col^f, 0} = 0. But for r = 1 the stacked tensor T^(f) is a single slice and its rank-one decomposition is trivially unique, so r(f) ≥ 1; the stated value is false. The proof's remaining case ('deg X > r ... intersects X in more than r real points') does not apply when X is linear (deg X = 1 = r at r = n_codim^f + 1), so the boundary case is neither proved nor correctly stated.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict Theorem 4.2 to tuples f for which X is nondegenerate (at least two unit entries, or a single entry f_i >= 2), and state the degenerate cases separately with their correct value (r(f) = 1); recompute the affected entries of Corollary cor:r_max_with_matching. No main conclusion is lost.
issues.overall_effect: Theorem 4.2 returns r(f) = 0 for degenerate flattening tuples although uniqueness holds at r = 1; Corollary cor:r_max_with_matching, whose formulas combine r(f), r(f') and r(d-f) via Theorem 4.2, inherits these wrong values, understating the recoverable rank in regimes where a partner tuple is degenerate.
issues.title: r(f) formula in Theorem on maximal rank is false for degenerate flattenings
issues.why_classification: A local exclusion/patch of degenerate tuples preserves every advertised guarantee and all comparisons among nondegenerate flattenings; no new argument beyond restating the boundary case is required.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Multiplying the equations \eqref{eq:vw} with the Hermitian transposes $\fv^H$ and $\fw^H$ respectively, and setting

Note that $\beta_1,\beta_2$ are real non-negative numbers with $\beta_1 + \beta_2\leq 1$ since the symmetric matrices $\frac{\mathbf{H}_{1,1}}{\alpha_1} + \mathbf{P}_1, \frac{\mathbf{H}_{2,2}}{\alpha_2}+\mathbf{P}_2$ have eigenvalues in $[0,1]$ and $\|\fv\|^2 +  \|\fw \|^2 = 1$.

issues.failure_explanation: Multiplying the two equations of (eq:vw) by v^H and w^H gives lambda*||v||^2 = beta_1 + mu/alpha_1 and lambda*||w||^2 = (lambda/alpha_2)*conj(mu) + beta_2. The proof replaces these by lambda = beta_1 + mu/alpha_1 and lambda = (lambda/alpha_2)*conj(mu) + beta_2, which is valid only if ||v|| = ||w|| = 1; but the same proof uses the eigenvector normalization ||v||^2 + ||w||^2 = 1, so the two normalizations are incompatible (unless one block vanishes, a case the argument does not handle). Every later step of the spectrum analysis - the reality of lambda, the case split on mu, and the final bound lambda < (max{alpha_1,alpha_2}-mu)/(alpha_1+alpha_2-mu) < 1 - is derived from these two flawed scalar relations, so the spectral-radius claim rho(JPsi) < 1, and with it the stated local linear convergence, is unestablished.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Redo the eigenvalue analysis of J Psi on the tangent space of the product of spheres with a consistent normalization (handling the cases w = 0 and v = 0 separately); the hypotheses already assumed (block convexity, sigma > 0, second-order criticality) suffice for this contained recomputation, after which the stated conclusion holds unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: Proposition prop:local linear (local linear convergence of PS-HOPM to second-order critical pSVTs in the two-block case) is unproven; the paper's advertised local convergence guarantee for two-block tensors, including its application to T-tilde^(f), is unsupported.
issues.title: Spectral analysis in local linear convergence proof drops eigenvector norms
issues.why_classification: The repair is a contained re-derivation of one spectral estimate using only assumptions already in place - no new global proof architecture and no loss of the stated guarantee - but it is more than a local slip because the central spectral estimates must be re-established with a corrected normalization.

issues.failure_explanation: The displayed equality gives |mu_i - <R^(i), T_w>| = |sum_{j != i} mu_j <R^(j), R^(i)>| <= rho * sum_{j!=i} |mu_j| <= (r-1) rho ||mu||_inf, not <= rho||mu||_inf; the dropped factor (r-1) matters for every r >= 3. Hence the subsequent bound ||mu||_inf <= max_i|<R^(i), T_w>|/(1-rho) does not follow (the valid estimate is with 1-(r-1)rho in the denominator, which additionally requires (r-1)rho < 1). The theorem's upper bound F_Acal <= C * max_i |<R^(i), T_w>| with the stated constant C = (1-rho)^{-1}(prod_k (1+(r-1)rho_k))^{1/ell} is therefore not established by the proof, and is unsupported for r >= 3 with large coherence.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the inequality to |mu_i - <R^(i), T_w>| <= (r-1) rho ||mu||_inf, obtaining F_Acal <= ((prod_k (1+(r-1)rho_k))^{1/ell})/(1-(r-1)rho) * max_i |<R^(i), T_w>| under the additional condition (r-1)rho < 1, and restate the theorem with this constant and condition.
issues.overall_effect: The upper bound of Theorem thm:added-2 (and the two-sided control of F_Acal used to interpret possibly suboptimal critical points) is unproven for r >= 3; the accompanying remark on the near-orthogonal case is unaffected, but the stated constant cannot be relied upon.
issues.title: Upper bound in Theorem on objective function uses an invalid inequality; constant C unsupported
issues.why_classification: A local one-step correction plus a limited weakening (worse constant, one added coherence condition) restores a comparable two-sided guarantee; no new lemma or global re-architecture is needed, but a substantive part of the stated bound (the constant, unconditional validity) is withdrawn.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let $\Acal=\Span\Bigl\{\,\bigotimes_{j=1}^\ell (\fv_{i}^{(j)})^{\otimes d_j}\ :\ 1\leq i\leq r\,\Bigr\}$, where the vectors $\fv_{i}^{(j)}$ are generic with norm one, and assume $\dim \Acal = r$.

Then \(\Vect(\mathscr{R}^{(i)}_{(d-f)})\) is the unique left singular vector of 
\(\mathbf{M}\) with
singular value \(1\) that is a vectorization of a rank-one tensor.

issues.failure_explanation: The tensors R^(i)_(f) have type f, while A is spanned by type-d tensors and f is not in {0,(d_1,...,d_l)} by hypothesis; so R^(i)_(f) is not an element of A at all and the quoted claim is ill-typed. The step the proof actually needs - that A contains no rank-one type-d tensor other than the r summands R^(l)_(d) - is a genuine identifiability statement about the type-(d) Segre-Veronese variety (governed, e.g., by the threshold of Theorem 4.2 applied with tuple d), which is neither among the hypotheses nor proved; the invoked bound r <= r(f) concerns the f-flattening and does not imply it. Without it, a rank-one element W of A outside the r summands would produce a left singular vector of M with singular value 1 distinct from Vect(R^(i)_(d-f)), so the stated uniqueness is unsupported.

failure_location.quote: Moreover, the $r$ rank-one tensors $\{\mathscr{R}^{(i)}_{(f)}\}_{i=1}^r$ are the only rank-one elements in $\Acal$ (up to scale), since $r \leq r(f)$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the missing hypothesis that A contains exactly the r rank-one type-d tensors up to scale (equivalently, r below the uniqueness threshold for the type-(d) flattening as in Theorem 4.2), and re-derive the formulas of Corollary cor:r_max_with_matching with the additional minimum; the surviving guarantees cover a restricted but comparable regime.
issues.overall_effect: Theorem 6.2's uniqueness conclusion is unproven; Corollary cor:r_max_with_matching (items on symmetry-breaking and paired flattenings) and Corollary cor:added-1 (optimal flattenings for (ell,1)-tensors), which apply it, inherit the gap, so the advertised recovery ranks for those flattenings are unsupported.
issues.title: Matching theorem's uniqueness step is ill-typed and relies on an unestablished identifiability condition
issues.why_classification: The repair requires imposing a new, substantive hypothesis (or proving the type-(d) uniqueness statement) and weakening the affected r_max formulas by an additional minimum, but no new global proof architecture; a recognizably comparable result survives.

issues.failure_explanation: For the tuple f=(1,1) in S^4(R^n)(x)R^k with k = 2, f has two unit entries and min{n,k} = 2, so the exceptional branch of Theorem thm:rmax_formula applies: r(1,1) = min{n_col, n_codim+1} with n_col = binom(n+2,3) and n_codim + 1 = (n-1)(k-1)+1 = n, i.e. r(1,1) = min{binom(n+2,3), n} = n for n >= 2. The corollary's displayed case 'min{4,n}, k = 2' contradicts this (e.g. n = 5, k = 2 gives r(1,1) = 5, not 4); the two subcases n = 2 and k = 2 are also given inconsistent values when both hold.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the case 'min{4,n}, k = 2' by 'r(1,1) = min{binom(n+2,3), n} = n'; no other step or claim of the corollary changes.
issues.overall_effect: One displayed case value in the supporting computation of Corollary cor:added-1 is false; the corollary's final optimality conclusion is unaffected because the corrected value n still satisfies r(2,1) = binom(n+1,2) >= n, so (2,1) still dominates for k = 2.
issues.title: NA
issues.why_classification: A local correction of one case value, with the corollary's stated optimality conclusion and threshold surviving unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
Let \(\mathbf{O}_u,\mathbf{O}_v\in\RR^{r\times(r-1)}\) have orthonormal columns spanning
\(\Span\{\mathbf{C}\fa_u\}^\perp\) and \(\Span\{\mathbf{C}\fa_v\}^\perp\), respectively. Define
\[
 \hat{\mathbf{U}}:=\mathbf{U}\mathbf{O}_v,
\qquad \hat {\mathbf{C}}:=\mathbf{O}_u\T \mathbf{C} \mathbf{O}_v,\qquad \hat {\mathbf{V}}:=\mathbf{V}\mathbf{O}_u.
\]

issues.failure_explanation: The update formulas in item (2) are only valid in the symmetric/orthogonal setting of the cited source and are false for generic partially symmetric summands. Counterexample: T = 2 e1 (x) e1 (x) e1 + 3 ((e1+e2)/sqrt2) (x) e2 (x) e2 with f = (1,0,0) gives T^(f) = [[2,0,0,3/sqrt2],[0,0,0,3/sqrt2]], U = I2, V = [e1,e4], C^(-1) = [[2,3/sqrt2],[0,3/sqrt2]]; fa_u = fa_v = e1, so O_u = O_v = e2 and the construction yields U-hat = e2, C-hat = sqrt2/3, lambda_1 = 2 (item (1) is correct). The true deflated flattening T - lambda_1 a1 b1^T has column span spanned by a2 = (e1+e2)/sqrt2, which U O_v = e2 does not span, and U-hat C-hat^(-1) V-hat^T = (3 sqrt2/2) e2 e4^T differs from the deflated matrix (whose (1,4)-entry is 3/sqrt2, not 0). Hence (2)(b) and (2)(c) fail: the columns of U-hat do not form an orthonormal basis of the remaining factors' span, so subsequent deflation rounds of Algorithm alg:psspm-deflation operate on a wrong subspace and compute wrong coefficients.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct item (2): the deflated column space is spanned by U times a basis of the complement appropriate to the remaining factors (in U-coordinates the complement of span{P_{.1}} where C^(-T) fa_u is proportional to the normal direction), with the matching V-update; alternatively, replace the closed-form update in item (2) and in Algorithm alg:psspm-deflation by a fresh rank factorization (e.g. SVD) of the explicitly deflated flattening T^(f) - lambda_1 Vect(R_(f)) Vect(R_(d-f))^T, which is routine and restores the stated guarantee.
issues.overall_effect: Proposition prop:deflation's items (2)(b) and (2)(c) are false for generic (non-orthogonal) summands, and the Deflation step of Algorithm alg:psspm-deflation, which performs exactly these updates, computes wrong bases and coefficients for later rounds; the guaranteed full decomposition of the main algorithm fails precisely in the generic asymmetric regimes the paper targets (item (1), the scalar lambda_1, remains correct).
issues.title: Deflation proposition's factor-update identities fail for generic partially symmetric tensors
issues.why_classification: A contained, supported resolution exists - replacing the crossed complement update by the correct Wedderburn deflation (or recomputing a rank factorization of the deflated flattening) - which preserves the algorithm's stated decomposition guarantee and all downstream claims at a minor efficiency cost; no new proof architecture and no advertised regime is lost, but the specific update formulas as promised are withdrawn, so the issue is more than minor.
